newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-MEXICAN OFFICIAL RESIGNS AFTER MILUTINOVIC STAYS ON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MEXICAN OFFICIAL RESIGNS AFTER MILUTINOVIC STAYS ON.

text.p: A leading Mexican soccer official has resigned after the federation ignored his advice to sack national team coach Bora Milutinovic.
Enrique Borja, president of the Mexican federation's national team commission, stepped down in protest after members of the federation last week voted that Yugoslav Milutinovic should stay on.
Borja had earlier travelled to Argentina to offer Milutinovic's job to Carlos Bilardo who led Argentina to World Cup victory in 1986 and the runners-up spot in 1990.
Borja was unhappy after Mexico suffered humiliating defeats by Honduras and Jamaica in World Cup qualifying matches.
Despite the defeats Mexico still made it to the final six-team stage of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers which will be held next year to decide the region's three representatives in France in 1998.
Milutinovic coached Mexico in the 1986 World Cup when they hosted the tournament and reached the quarter-finals.
